title: One-bit slice sum as a one-bit inner product
statement:
Fix a real number $\rho$, Boolean functions $f, g : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, and points $x', y' \in \{0,1\}^n$. For a bit $b$, write $(x', b)$ for the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by appending $b$ as the last coordinate of $x'$, and let $\sigma$ denote the sign encoding. Then
\[
  \frac12 \sum_{b \in \{0,1\}} \sum_{b' \in \{0,1\}}
    \frac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(b)\,\sigma(b')}{2}\,
    f(x', b)\, g(y', b')
  \;=\;
  \langle F,\; T_\rho G\rangle,
\]
where $F, G : \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ are the one-bit slices $F(t) = f(x', t_0)$ and $G(t) = g(y', t_0)$, and the inner product and the noise operator $T_\rho$ are taken on the one-dimensional cube $\{0,1\}^1$.
hypotheses_covered: ρ is an arbitrary real number
f and g are real-valued Boolean functions on the (n+1)-cube
x' and y' are points of the n-cube
the slices F, G and the operators live on the one-bit cube {0,1}^1
replaced:
Fix $x', y' \in \mathrm{BoolCube}\,n$ and $f, g : \mathrm{BoolCube}\,(n+1) \to \bbr$. The
one-bit kernel-weighted sum of the slices of $f$ at $x'$ and of $g$ at $y'$ equals the one-bit
inner product of those slices against the noise operator:
\[
  \tfrac12 \sum_{b}\sum_{b'} \tfrac{1+\rho\,\chi(b)\chi(b')}{2}\,
  f(\mathrm{snoc}(x',b))\, g(\mathrm{snoc}(y',b'))
  \;=\;
  \inn{f_{x'}, T_\rho g_{y'}},
\]
where $f_{x'}(t) = f(\mathrm{snoc}(x', t_0))$ and $g_{y'}(t) = g(\mathrm{snoc}(y', t_0))$ are
functions on $\mathrm{BoolCube}\,1$.
